title: Decompose Program.cs into named registration/pipeline modules with a testable external-auth callback
description:
Audit #9 (audits/hyperagent-audit-9-architecture-deepening-20260611), candidate 1 — Strong; top recommendation.

### Problem
Program.cs is an 862-line linear script with no seams: ~30 service registrations, the OpenTelemetry block, the exception-handler and security-header lambdas, request logging, two page-asset endpoint handlers, and a 185-line GitHub OAuth callback lambda (lines 133-317: user creation, provider-link management, role assignment, durable audit evidence) all live inline. Incident evidence: the June 4 reconstruction silently dropped ~16 blocks (security headers, exception handler, request logging, OTel, the settings-override load) and ran that way for a week. The OAuth callback is pinned only by TagGovernanceTests.ExternalAuthCallbacks_RecordDurableSuccessAndFailureEvidence, a source-inspection test that greps Program.cs for symbol names as text - it passes even with the code commented out.

### Approach
- Named registration modules: AddMemorySmithStorage / AddMemorySmithSecurity / AddMemorySmithChat / AddMemorySmithMaintenance / AddMemorySmithTelemetry (extension methods, one file each under MemorySmith.App/Hosting)
- UseMemorySmithPipeline extension owning middleware order (exception handler, security headers, request logging)
- Extract the GitHub OAuth callback into an external-auth callback module with a fake-ticket-testable interface; replace the text-grep test with real unit tests on the module (keep a thin wiring assertion if desired)
- Extract the page-asset endpoints (path sanitization + authorization) into their own module with unit tests
- Program.cs becomes a composition root (~100 lines) of visible call lines

### Acceptance criteria
- Behavior-preserving: full suite green; AppApiContractTests pipeline assertions (problem+json traceId, security headers, request-log correlation) pass unchanged
- The OAuth callback has direct unit tests covering success recording, link-conflict / disabled-user failure recording, and role assignment - no text-grep needed for evidence recording
- Dropping any registration/pipeline module from Program.cs is visible as a one-line diff
- DI conventions preserved (explicit factories where constructor selection is ambiguous)

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Implemented. Program.cs is now an 88-line composition root; each concern is a named module under MemorySmith.App/Hosting: ConfigurationSetup (secrets + the admin settings-override layer the June 4 incident dropped), SerilogSetup, SecuritySetup (cookie + OAuth wiring, policies, rate limits, data protection), GitHubOAuthCallbackHandler (the extracted 185-line callback - now a real seam), StorageSetup, CoreSetup, TelemetrySetup, ChatSetup, MaintenanceSetup, PipelineSetup (middleware order documented as load-bearing), ContentEndpoints (page-asset path sanitization helpers now internal static + reachable for unit tests). Registration order and middleware order preserved exactly. The dishonest text-grep test was replaced: GitHubOAuthCallbackHandlerTests drives the handler with a real temp-file metadata DB, stubbed GitHub backchannel, and DefaultHttpContext, asserting DURABLE evidence (login-history rows, auth.login.succeeded/failed audit events, first-admin bootstrap, claims, ticket failure, remote-failure redirect). The TagGovernance assertion now only pins wiring. Suite: 511 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped (was 507; +4 behavioral OAuth tests).
